name: Jerry
long_description:
Your car and your home are your most expensive assets. And for most people, these aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair or, worse, an accident, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

Jerry is building the first AI agent to manage all your physical assets. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, and have been profitable since 2024. We're now expanding into home, motorcycle, RV, and beyond.

We’re fully remote with offices in Palo Alto, New York, Chicago, and Toronto.
one_liner: Jerry is building the AI agent to manage all your physical assets.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: My co-founders, Lina Zhang and Musawir Shah, and I worked together at my previous startup, YourMechanic, a company that provides mobile automotive repair and maintenance services to vehicle owners at their location. Through that experience and our own personal, frustrating experiences with all car ownership hassles, we knew this was a category ripe for disruption. From determining what car to buy, financing a vehicle, finding insurance, licensing, titles, warranties, repairs, parking, and maintenance, we saw very clearly that services for car owners were lagging behind the ease and convenience offered in other industries. We wanted to remove the friction and make the transactions seamless and less expensive. The three of us set out to launch a product that would solve these hassles for car owners. We started with a car insurance compare-and-buy service that quickly gained traction _Since then we have helped more than 3 million customers shop for car insurance. We’ve also expanded our vision from a car insurance shopping site to a car ownership super app. That is because car insurance is just one of the expensive hassles car owners experience. Today, in addition to our car insurance marketplace, our app helps customers with auto refinancing, safe driving and more._

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer: Owning a car is the second largest American household expense. And, so many components of car ownership are complicated and outdated, like buying insurance and refinancing an auto loan. It is a big problem because owning a car should make your life easier but in many ways it makes it more complicated. Through my own experience, I learned that owning a car is not the “American dream” I hoped it would be, but rather, it’s expensive, frustrating and time consuming.We decided to build a product that takes the frustration out of car ownership – starting with shopping for and buying insurance – and makes it easy to save. Through our AI-backed insurance marketplace, car owners can automatically shop from more than 55 top U.S. car insurance companies in 45 seconds and complete the transaction in minutes. This approach to revamping the insurance shopping experience worked and it saves Jerry customers, on average, more than $800 per year.We applied this same automated technology to our auto refinancing marketplace, which takes a typical end-to-end process of 19 days down to less than 48 hours. And our goal is to shrink that even further. _Through insurance and refinancing we’ve started solving the small problems that contribute to the massive frustration that is car ownership in the U.S._

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: The long term vision is to create a car ownership super app that supports drivers with all their expensive car hassles, saving them both time and money. Today, we do that through our car insurance and auto refinancing marketplaces, and we offer customers rewards for safe driving with our Drive Well, Earn Perks program. But these aren’t the only expenses drivers incur, which means there are many other opportunities for Jerry to support our customers, with things like maintenance, parking, and more._We want to solve all of those issues. When drivers no longer have to worry about car ownership hassles because they know Jerry is doing the work to save them time and money, we will have achieved our goal._

name: Goodcover
long_description:
Goodcover provides its Members with Good Renters Insurance for 50% less than legacy companies and an Annual Dividend of the money left over after claims obligations are met.

Goodcover is a Managing General Agent (MGA) that administers personal insurance on behalf of our Membership, a bit like how USAA does it.

Member's premiums are pooled and used to pay claims.  We take a fixed fee, and the remainder is returned in our Annual Member Dividend.

We work with multi-billion dollar capital partners to ensure regulations are followed, adequate claims capital is always available, and we have emergency capacity for catastrophes.

Technology allows us to eliminate waste, saving roughly 25% of the cost.  We are 100% digital, but not bots - we invest in tech that enables our experts to help Members.

As an Invitation Only Membership served by an MGA, **we can give Members Free Insurance** when they invite others, turning our "Marketing Budget" into savings for Members.  This eliminates Lizards and Sales Agents, saving the other 25%.
We do not use the standard industry models, instead using a multiperil model to more granularly price risk.  This means that for a few of you we are more expensive... but everyone else pays much less than they would otherwise pay.

Our granular, multiperil model allows us to offer a superior policy over the standard market including:
    - coverage for if your place is flooded by a neighbor
    - Replacement Cost Coverage (meaning new stuff for your old)
    - All Risk coverage for high value items you tell us about - including computers (almost no one does that amazingly)
    - added coverage for mold removal

Our MGA business model allows us to be capital efficient, "renting" capacity as we need it.

All this adds up to our government approved pricing being 40-60% cheaper on average than that of our competitors.
one_liner: Digital Co-op Renters Insurance = half the price, better coverage.

launches.body:
Happy Friday YC Family,

Today, we launched The New Normal, our new bi-weekly video show featuring the enterprise leaders actually deploying AI in production at scale. This 51 second video features one of our first customers graduating over 90,000 learners per year:

Sizzle clip: <https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7475888904307605504/>

And you can watch the full episode where he goes into detail about the use cases he has in production with us here:

Full Episode 1 with Kermit Cook (CEO, Penn Foster): <https://youtu.be/r8ge3VbVFoA>

Backstory:

My Co-Founder, Timur Meyster and I went through YC W19 building what became Career Karma, the largest career transition platform for people from non-traditional backgrounds breaking into tech. We made thousands of customer calls personally and managed third-party BPOs at scale. We learned the customer experience operating model from the inside.

The thing we kept seeing across our enterprise partners was the same. Customer experience teams stuck in reactive, inbound-first models. Tools that waited for the customer to raise a hand. And the customers who needed the most help were the ones least likely to do that on their own.

We pivoted to OutRival in 2024 to build the opposite. Over the last two years we have sat with more than 300 enterprise leaders across higher education, insurance, travel, and beyond, iterating alongside the operators running the work. Digital Workers that take the first move. That can run millions of outreach attempts a month across voice, text, and email, with the compliance posture a regulated enterprise needs. That can be onboarded into a team like a new hire.

The Show:

The New Normal is co-hosted by me, Timur, and our Head of Insurance John Henry. All three of us have built media at scale before. Timur and I previously hosted Breaking Into Startups, which reached more than 3 million people. John Henry previously hosted Hustle on VICELAND, executive produced by Alicia Keys and Marcus Samuelsson, which reached tens of millions. John is also a co-founder of Harlem Capital and Loop.

This time the centerpiece is our customers and the operators inside them actually deploying AI at scale.

As mentioned earlier, Episode 1 is with Kermit Cook (CEO, Penn Foster). Confirmed cohort going forward includes Presidents of WGU, Miami Dade, UMGC, SNHU, NU, and OU; CEOs of DeVry, Cengage, and Campus; plus senior leaders at University of Phoenix and UMass Global. More coming across insurance and travel.

15 episodes scheduled. 7 already recorded. Bi-weekly cadence starts today.

1\. Operators for The New Normal show. We're recording 15-30 more episodes over the next 3-4 months across higher ed, insurance, and travel. If you know an executive operator at a Fortune 1000 company running real outbound AI deployments inside their org and generating revenue, send them my way.

Thanks for reading. Hit me on Bookface or at [ruben@outrival.com](mailto:ruben@outrival.com).

Indian employers are dissatisfied with their health benefits today because insurance in India only covers hospital stays, not doctor visits – and only 8% of their employees will ever use the benefit in the year. With Loop, employers can offer a more engaging health benefit that includes doctor visits and telemedicine, alongside traditional hospital coverage, for about the same price. launches.tagline: Multimodal AI employees that see, speak, think and run operations
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Nuha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nuhahashem/) and [Alok](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alokhk/) from [Cozmo AI](https://cozmox.ai?utm_source=yc-launch&utm_medium=listing&utm_campaign=launch).

**TL;DR** 

We help banks, insurers and lenders deploy multimodal AI employees that interpret documents and videos, speak with customers in real time, think using your policies and do the work in your core systems.

Check out our [launch video](https://youtu.be/IGypdMioyIo).

**❌ The problem**

If you’ve ever seen how a real customer operation gets handled inside a large company, you’ll notice the conversation is usually the shortest part. Most of the time goes into opening 6-10 tools, finding history, checking documents, verifying details and recording what happened afterwards.

We ran into such issues while building a fintech product and spending months embedded with support and operations teams. A support case that looked “simple” from the outside often meant 40 minutes of prep and follow-up wrapped around an 8-minute customer interaction. The work was more around moving data and decisions across messy systems than actually talking to customers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/df0f9156-23c1-46c6-b05f-93060b590053)

To handle these cases, we built an internal system that could understand a case end-to-end and take actions across systems automatically. During a demo, a partner stopped us and asked for that system instead of the fintech product itself.

That became Cozmo.

**✅ How Cozmo is solving it**

Cozmo is a system of work for complex enterprise operations, starting with financial services and insurance. Companies use Cozmo to build and deploy AI employees, which are a collection of agents that own workflows end to end. They talk to customers, read documents, interpret videos, apply company policies and update systems like Guidewire, Temenos and Salesforce, pulling humans into the loop only when real judgment or escalation is needed.

Every decision the AI employee makes is logged, including its reasoning and policy reference, providing a complete audit trail for compliance and operations without additional manual effort. This is managed by our proprietary Agent Protocol Engine (APE), the control layer that keeps shared context, enforces policy and ensures every step is tracked for regulated industries.

Cozmo is live with 10+ enterprises, including Fortune Global 500s like Nestlé, and has already handled over 1M production calls and 10M interactions; cutting costs by up to 70% and turning roughly 1 in 13 conversations into revenue.

[Watch Cozmo in action.](https://youtu.be/ek8eE1bXOnU)

**🧬 What’s unique about Cozmo**

Most AI tools are just prompt trees with a UI. They’re fine for neat, repetitive tasks; but they fall apart the moment operations get messy, ending in half‑filled tickets, off‑script collection calls and disputes scattered across systems.

Cozmo is built for that mess:

* **Multimodal by default:** One platform to spin up AI employees that handle inbound and outbound calls, read PDFs and scanned forms, understand video and talk to customers in a single, continuous flow.
* **Runs on intent, not prompts:** You give it responsibilities and policies like a new hire, instead of maintaining endless prompt chains. As new case patterns appear, the AI employee adapts behavior without you rewriting a graph of scripts.
* **APE-powered coordination:** A single Cozmo “employee” is actually a coordinated team of agents, driven by our Agent Protocol Engine (APE), running an internal loop: planning, delegating, checking and rechecking across systems until the case is closed, not just until a workflow box is ticked.

So instead of a scripted bot, you get something that behaves much closer to a high‑performing operations hire: it keeps context, chases down loose ends and keeps pushing the work forward without you needing to orchestrate every move.

**🚀 Our story**

Nuha and Alok have been friends for over 11 years. We scaled a regulated fintech together in Dubai, navigating one of the most demanding regulatory environments in the world. When the regulations and market changed, we were forced to shut it down. We built AI employees to manage the fintech ourselves on cockroach mode, handling communications and documentation across every affected account. 

That system worked, and when a partner saw it, they asked to buy it instead. So we moved from Dubai to San Francisco to build Cozmo. 

Three years, two countries, 180 pivot, and we’re still going.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/4501b459-03fa-4135-9389-d407946bd5ec)

 🎯 **Our Ask**

We’re onboarding new enterprise customers in financial services and insurance. If you (or someone you know) run claims, collections or large-scale operations at a bank or insurer, we’d love to connect.

Employees are not offered personal and inclusive benefits that have an impact, resulting in poor uptake, whilst often founders aren’t sure how to engage their global teams effectively.

* A marketplace fo recommendations and discounts of quality over quantity
* Community benefits, connect over shared benefits within slack
* Personal and inclusive employee profiles for impactful recommendations
* Manager engagement budgets with prompts and reminders for employee gifting

Many of our users, who we like to call Happling’s (we’re working on that) have employees in many regions and simply want to consolidate their benefit allowance and roll it out with ease. Others want to make sure they’re getting the best prices and save money through benchmarking.

We support start-ups from 5 employees or more, all the way through to more mature companies with thousands of employees like Google, NatWest Bank, The Metropolitan Police, and more.

Hey there 👋 We’re [@Eric Yen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yeneric/) & [@Eilam Levitov](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eilamlevitov/) founders of [Stream](https://www.stream.claims/) (S22).

**tl;dr**

The two of us are insurance and tech veterans innovating in commercial insurance claims. At Stream we automate the high-touch workflows workers’ comp claims adjusters do on a daily basis. Our platform saves adjuster time spent on repetitive tasks like calling and faxing, allowing the adjuster to focus on the high-value claim activities that improve the injured workers’ claim experience and optimize financial outcomes for insurance companies.

**The Problem** 🤕

Workers’ Compensation (WC) insurance is a government-mandated program that provides benefits to workers who get hurt on the job. When a workplace injury occurs, a claim is filed on behalf of the injured worker. This claim pays out for the wages and medical treatment needed to get the employee back to work.

Today, claim adjudication is a grossly manual process which involves adjusters spending the majority of their day either on the phone tracking down information or entering unstructured notes into legacy systems. The average adjuster handles 140 cases at any single time and takes 5 business days to respond to inquiries from injured workers.

Consequently, the Injured worker is left alone to navigate an unfamiliar and complex claims process. Imagine feeling vulnerable with no clue how your bills will be paid. This pushes injured workers to the brink and inevitably to the front door of their local injury lawyer. In states like CA & FL, over one third of all WC claims are litigated - and the moment an attorney gets involved, that claim balloons 5x in cost.

**\~ Stream**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65582&key=user_uploads/986387/9172c9b2-5a9e-4064-80b6-d180a335c129)

The two of us met at Next Insurance, where Eric led WC product and Eilam led Risk Engineering. Eric also previously worked at Liberty Mutual as a WC claims adjuster for 5 years. At Next, we realized nothing has changed since Eric’s days as an adjuster and none of the automation we were building for the underwriting side exists in claims management today. That’s why we left to build Stream.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65582&key=user_uploads/986387/9c055997-8925-4c23-b75b-7117213d6550)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65582&key=user_uploads/986387/b33699f2-0c61-43aa-a3fc-a98ddeca5c3f)

Stream saves up to 40% of an adjuster’s time spent on the phone, sending faxes, and manually typing notes into their claim system. Moreover, we also improve the claim experience for the injured worker by providing real-time information such as claim status and financial updates, and help facilitate services such as transportation to doctors offices - all via text.

Thanks,

Eric & Eilam

launches.body:
#  Coverage Cat AI Insurance Bench

We’re Coverage Cat. We built an AI insurance benchmark to measure how frontier models perform on real insurance workflows, not trivia or generic reasoning tasks.

### TL;DR

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106902&key=user_uploads/123258/e54c9091-f0a5-4500-b9f8-125255d46418)

Coverage Cat’s AI Insurance Benchmark compares 7 frontier models on two insurance-specific evals:

* Price estimation: can a model estimate umbrella insurance quote ranges accurately?
* Brokerage/Agent task: can a model answer practical insurance questions the way a good broker or agent would?

The public leaderboard ranks models by Elo Rating, Win Rate, Quote Coverage, Quote MAPE, Winkler Loss, and judged brokerage-task quality.

View it here: Coverage Cat AI Insurance Benchmark (<https://www.coveragecat.com/ai/leaderboard>)

### The Problem

Most AI benchmarks don’t tell you whether a model is useful inside a real insurance workflow or whether consumers can really trust it for insurance information.

Insurance work is full of messy edge cases: pricing uncertainty, underwriting rules, coverage terminology, household risk factors, and questions where the answer needs to be both correct and concise.

There has been good prior work on insurance AI benchmarks, including UNDERWRITE, which evaluates multi-turn underwriting agents with domain experts, noisy tools, and simulated users. That work focuses on enterprise underwriting agent behavior and found meaningful gaps between general model performance and enterprise readiness.

Our benchmark is different: it focuses on consumer insurance workflows Coverage Cat actually needs to automate, including umbrella quote estimation and broker/agent-style answers. It is also designed as a public, continuously updated leaderboard rather than a one-time research benchmark.

### What We Built

The first public version includes:

* 2,800+ price-estimation scenarios
* 19,000+ quote model results
* 1,200+ brokerage/agent task questions
* 8900+ QA model results
* 7 tested models

The benchmark uses anonymized eval data, no-retention/no-logging model platforms, and aggregate-only public snapshots. Customer data is not exposed to model providers.

### What’s Next

We’ll update the leaderboard soon with newer frontier models as they become available through our approved model-provider paths. We also expect to expand the benchmark with more brokerage workflows, richer human review, and additional insurance product lines.

Our goal is simple: make it obvious which AI models are actually good at insurance work and help those models improve.

View the leaderboard: Coverage Cat AI Insurance Benchmark (<https://www.coveragecat.com/ai/leaderboard>)

If you’re shopping for umbrella coverage, you can also start here: Coverage Cat Umbrella Insurance (<https://www.coveragecat.com/insurance-types/umbrella-insurance>).

# **Intro**

I’m Aman and we’re building Mulligan, the world’s first end-to-end AI automation platform for commercial insurance brokers. It automates Quoting, Policy Comparison, Proposals, Commissions and more. We work with dozens of brokers and have helped all of them scale their businesses without adding more employees.

# **Problem**

Selling and servicing commercial insurance is a complicated process to begin with, and the manual paperwork involved makes it difficult to scale profitably. Brokers have to spend hours reading lengthy documents, navigating ancient portals and formatting documents to fit into their internal systems.

Existing automation tools typically only address narrow workflows and do not integrate with each other, which means that automating a brokerage involves juggling multiple solutions and integrations.

The end result is that brokerages spend hundreds of hours every week, and billions of dollars annually, on non-revenue generating tasks and outsourcing.

# **Solution**

Mulligan assembles submissions, generates quotes from carrier portals, compares quotes and policies, generates proposals and handles commission statements in minutes, without needing your hands-on-keyboard. Here’s what it can do:

### **Quoting**

Quote from one of the largest selections of commercial lines insurance carriers for Commercial Auto, Workers’ Compensation, Business Owners’, General Liability and Trucking policies. Do so with minimal data entry and largely without human intervention. This makes it easy for an agent to get a more complete view of the market, do less data entry and spend more time with their customers.

To use it, select the carriers to quote, upload any documents that contain relevant data and click “Submit’’. Mulligan then logs into and produces draft quotes in each carrier portal, ready to review, edit and bind.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94819&key=user_uploads/1013488/6f26d394-1c38-4f97-a17e-99c397e184db)

### **Policy Checking & Comparison**

Analyze quotes, binders or policies, compare across documents and identify gaps in coverage. Manually analyzing these documents used to take hours, if not days, and can now be done in minutes. This tool can be used to service existing customers, as well as to help close new ones by analyzing their existing policies and identifying areas of improvement.

Simply upload docs, view them side-by-side, chat with them and match them to checklists to identify gaps.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94819&key=user_uploads/1013488/dbc87031-968d-4c02-8301-d77ee5cd94d3)

### **Proposals**

Generate beautiful, branded proposals using quotes, policies and binders in minutes. These documents can be produced in Mulligan’s own design format, or using a template provided by the agency. The end result is a document whose style, content and tone showcases the agency’s professionalism and thoroughness.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94819&key=user_uploads/1013488/f393c554-a4f4-4485-8d9a-9e89bfe6248e)

### **Submissions**

Produce clean, complete and professional submissions to send to underwriters. Upload diverse documents such as loss runs, SOVs, vehicle and driver lists, and produce easily ingestible documents with just a few clicks. These submissions help portray the customer in the best possible light, and get processed by underwriters faster since they are well organized and easy to process.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94819&key=user_uploads/1013488/66ba3d38-9f05-4ae9-a64f-fccefee61a2c)

### **Commissions**

Extract commissions from lengthy statements and transform them into a format expected by most popular Agency Management Systems such as Applied Epic, AMS360, EZLynx, Veruna and more. Furthermore, review the values in the commission statement to check if there’s an underpayment from the carrier, or to reconcile the books faster.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94819&key=user_uploads/1013488/218d7bc3-1aa4-45d6-abb8-0ddabd48c31f)

# **🧨 Problem: Regulated notices are tedious and high-risk.**

For claims teams, state departments of insurance typically have very clear guidelines around the specific types of notices an insurer is supposed to provide to the parties involved. These include notices like claim acknowledgment, status updates, proactive reservations of rights, and finally, either a claim denial, partial denial, or settlement letter detailing what finally is or isn’t covered.

While that may seem straightforward, many organizations fail to meet these requirements as adjustors struggle to efficiently write notices up to the required quality bar. Numerous carriers we’ve talked to and currently work with have audited their claims organizations and found that their teams spend upwards of **30% of their working hours** just handling these notices.

Why? Many times, these notices end up in a court of law where an unhappy claimant will sue the insurer, arguing that the notice was ambiguous.

# **🎉 Solution: One platform to consolidate, collaborate, and send notices.**

Kyber’s LetterGen helps companies streamline their notice creation process, removing tedious overhead and minimizing risk from claimants suing companies for acting in bad faith.

Most of these tasks have remained manual for two reasons:

* The insurance industry operates on a lot of unstructured data like policies, quotes & more
* The software systems in the insurance industry are not connected, requiring humans to manually fill in data and forms across these systems.

Previously, it was not possible to process the unstructured data with high accuracy, and it was difficult to configure all the validation rules. To make things worse, Robotic Process Automation was too brittle to maintain.

These manual workflows take the time of the skilled workforce away from the important tasks, reducing productivity and job satisfaction.

One such manual workflow is quote generation: a mid-sized (50-200 EEs) broker/MGA generates 1000s of quotes per month by extracting data from policy documents and then entering into portals. It takes about 30-45 mins per quote.

### **💡 SOLUTION**

At FurtherAI, we are building a AI Workspace to automate insurance workflows. These AI Teammates can practically automate any insurance workflow involving processing unstructured documents, data entry into internal systems or web portals, or even making phone calls.

[Here](https://youtu.be/nR-j_hTdgeI) is a quick demo of the AI Teammate performing Quote Generation. It is a simple workflow:

1\. **Trigger** - Send an email along with the client application attached

2\. **Clarification** - Respond to the missing information asked by AI

3\. **Result** - Get the generated quote along with the execution video

We are building these AI Teammates to mimic human-to-human interaction.

* Everything happens within the email client (Outlook/Gmail)

* We are building agentic loops to make the automation reliable

Our initial customers are saving over $400K in annual costs across these workflows while making them 10X faster and less prone to human errors. We are starting with the workflows of quote generation and renewals as they directly impact the top line of our customers.

launches.body:
\*\*TLDR: InQuery helps carriers, state funds, self-insured employers and TPAs automate tedious parts of the claims processing workflow so that claims can get closed faster and litigated less.\*\*\
\
Hey everyone, we’re [Erick](https://linkedin.com/in/erick-enriquez) and [Khalil](https://linkedin.com/in/khalil-miri?challengeId=AQHWHo0KU27KHgAAAYtAT5ChJwAxKyHDUTBZ_lM6cVviquDDjRyqB9xJxhlm0ATSXVRSaWgd29Ey0nUP_7m83XuDx3BvDkY4Jw&submissionId=2e9e84f8-0d0e-8f17-0b3e-f45c8158d27c&challengeSource=AgHqCrfI9npr2QAAAYtAT8XC638RucWqcGTLCZ7eovbJ-AYf7th1Rp30ur3XDSY&challegeType=AgHlTtcDd_2XCAAAAYtAT8XEcBz-r74sxX0ukDxvpdpO-N0f--z8dVw&memberId=AgFc2--6eoHdUwAAAYtAT8XHLvuvaBS3QEThr7PWG6--ydU&recognizeDevice=AgExDFN6a2fGlAAAAYtAT8XJR2ljtKp39iqIOlBAMno1-CUSmezV) and we’re building [InQuery](https://www.inquery.ai/). \
\
**🔍 Problem**\
The insurance industry is facing a labor shortage that is creating a negative spiral for staffing. As carriers struggle to hire, existing talent is getting overloaded and under-trained, causing severe retention issues at most large carriers. This talent squeeze means that per-case performance quality drops, leading claimants to experience confusion and frustration, which inevitably drives litigation rates upwards as they seek representation and support. As a result, average claim costs are rising, squeezing carriers expense ratios at the same time as inflation causes ballooning medical costs. 

Still, claims adjusters like my sister spend most of their day transcribing telephone calls, navigating large sets of semi-structured policies, and mapping data from large and complicated medical documents to relatively structured schemas in their existing CMS.

**🦾 Our Solution**

At InQuery, our mission is to develop AI agents tailored for the insurance industry, beginning with with claims handling. These agents will enable claims handlers to concentrate on high-impact settlement strategies, effective negotiations, and casualty remediation processes. The result? Reduced litigation rates, improved loss ratios, and enhanced satisfaction for both employees and claimants.

But our vision doesn’t stop there. As we perfect our AI solutions for claims handling, we’re poised to expand into other insurance-specific workflows, bringing efficiency and innovation to every corner of the industry. Our AI agents will seamlessly integrate with your current team, taking over repetitive tasks and collaborating with human staff where their expertise is needed most. Join us in redefining insurance processes and empowering your workforce to achieve more.\
\
\*\*👋 About us:\*\*\
Before starting InQuery, we’ve been best friends since living in the same dorm during our freshman year studying Computer Science at Stanford.

![](https://lh7-us.googleusercontent.com/krqSs7LIAO18m20ptblmaz74UhYwXwAMIHwY22ZLG4orANZ2GRjnjk9U_mmiBdOVwR2KlSvdH0StCYadIwufhj2T3V8cv7o5q3BHT04hsA_F_aMm-uN6mHA_-OdQJG8axjRNS3tZVuqGZg7vAhMJkcE)

\
**Our Ask**\
If you or anyone you know has experienced the pain of handling claim caseloads of upwards 100+ active cases, we’d love to chat. We’re looking for intros to carriers, self-insured employers, and TPAs. \
\
Even if our product isn’t the right fit for you yet, we’d love to learn about what’s working well and what’s broken at your organization and share what we’ve learned from talking to dozens of carriers ourselves.

launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re [**Pascal**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pascal-wieler/) and [**Ken**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ken-hendricks-96181611a/), here to introduce you to [**Basepilot**](https://www.basepilot.com/).

# **TL;DR:**

Basepilot creates AI assistants to automate repetitive and manual work across a browser. We help companies save 30% of their time weekly and cut costs, freeing up resources for more high-value tasks. For example, finance, recruitment, or sales teams can automate mundane back-office tasks within a few clicks and a quick demonstration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79264&key=user_uploads/842820/08fef875-2fb5-427c-a017-7cf356bd6ed7)

# **Where Basepilot can help you:**

* **Sales** - To help automate sales outreach, prospecting, and follow-ups.
* **Recruitment** - To help with sourcing candidates and clients, and analyzing and triaging profiles.
* **Finance** - To help fill in applications/forms, transfer data, do accounting ops, and update customer details.
* & any other manual task across your browser!

# **Problem - 30% of a business’s total time and resources is wasted on mundane repetitive work**

Currently, businesses employ teams of knowledge workers (in sales, ops, recruitment, finance, and more) that face a lot of manual and repetitive processes that slow them down. Although critical to get done, these tasks take hours away from doing more high-value work leading to frustration and lower output among teams.

**For a business, this results in:**

* 30% of their team’s time wasted on mindless tasks
* Wasted resources spent on hiring more people to handle the workload
* Increased error rates through manual boring work

For example, a recruitment firm spends 8+ hours/week per recruiter on repetitive admin work to source candidates, analyze applications and enter data, instead of talking to candidates!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79264&key=user_uploads/842820/e1bb23d2-968a-4748-be21-d45be443f4f1)

**Existing solutions suck!**

* Off-the-shelf tools often don’t work as workflows are very specific to a company.
* Automating processes with tools like UI Path is extremely expensive, requires specialist automation engineers and takes several weeks or months to set up.

# **Solution - Automate repetitive tasks in minutes**

Basepilot makes it super easy for a business to build and train their own AI employees, enabling anyone in the company to automate their mundane and repetitive work, freeing up time for more high-value tasks.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TxvHeF--NU4>

We designed Basepilot with these core principles in mind:

* **Works where you work:** Basepilot works across the tools you already use right in your browser as a Chrome extension. No need to adopt new tools or change your workflows.
* **Teach it like a human:** There’s no need to get technical or hire an expensive automation team, simply train your new assistant to complete work, just like you’d teach a human: by showing and telling.
* **Faster ROI (at lower cost):** Automate workflows in minutes, not weeks or months. Unlike traditional automation tools, Basepilot can get set up and operational in a fraction of the time & cost.
* **Keep control:** Basepilot operates in your tabs, allowing you to check in and see what’s happening in real-time while you focus on more high-value work, e.g. engaging in customer conversations while Basepilot sources new leads in the background.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79264&key=user_uploads/842820/ce3bce79-8335-4901-9c9d-b6cd949a410b)

# **Meet Ken & Pascal 🇳🇿🇩🇪➡️🇺🇸**

[**Pascal**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pascal-wieler/) & [**Ken**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ken-hendricks-96181611a/) both independently traveled to San Francisco in the summer of 2023 (from Germany & New Zealand respectively). We came here without knowing each other to explore the startup space and build the future 💪🏼🔨🚀. While in SF, we met through common friends, vibed well, and started working together. We moved across the world to work together in Europe, and got into YC - which brought us back to the city! Super grateful to be back! ❤️😍

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79264&key=user_uploads/842820/58e95fa6-361d-4a33-8ddb-a2a1fedf1e26)

We were inspired by the new wave of AI capabilities and are passionate about unlocking more human creativity by automating away the processes we all absolutely despise!

launches.tagline: Meet Numo, filling the trust gap between businesses and international contractors by handling compliance, KYC, and payment.
launches.body:
# Numo is like upside-down Deel

# TL;DR

[Numo](https://numohq.com/) verifies and credentials global contractors and lets them earn and hold the USD they get from working for American companies. When they need to spend it, we transfer money instantly to their local bank account.

**We launched last week, and have 105 contractors already live and onboarded on Numo, sending their first invoices.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/4a2d0978-bdb1-42d8-a223-5c8554db82a9)

# Problem

**Paying international contractors for short-term engagements is messy**. It’s full of remittance services whose brands are not conducive to trust or a professional environment and often look fraudulent to the uninformed. \
\
**For contractors, it’s even messier**. With expensive fees, slow transfer times, and fuzzy tax + compliance rules — we’ve seen our customers resort to funneling money through friends and families just to get paid. \
\
And the death blow for contractors is the hyperinflation many of their home currencies are experiencing. **Contractors work more every day for less money**. International contractors want to hold their funds in USD as long as they can, and then bring it back only when they need to spend.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/dd9fa8fc-a5f6-4452-840c-983c916dc798)

# Solution

So we built Numo:

1. Contractors can onboard and get verified, background checked, and launch their profiles.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/c7a8c8c3-c8e5-43b2-bb63-ca263a11ddbd)

2. Every invoice they send via Numo to their clients is paired with their verified profile.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/ac16cb72-92bc-4a04-b8ed-fe2d6201e7b2)

3. Their American clients get to pay the way they are most comfortable: ACH payment to a US bank account.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/a6370253-5288-4585-bc8d-545bacda9e58)

4. Contractors can hold the USD they make stateside until the moment they need to spend it locally. They can transfer funds to their local account within 20 seconds without excessive fees.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/224d13fc-c6ef-423f-8750-437d738673b6)

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/de06e012-08e5-4ac3-8728-4c67339ae615)


# We’re the team to build this

We all met working in the messy, terrible world of global telecom. We were the early operators at Hologram — a worldwide cellular network for IoT — taking the business from $0 to $20M ARR and through a successful Series B round.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/f8cd963f-353b-4bc5-8994-aaca6f3f0b83)

_👆 The Numo team on the ground running onboarding events in Lagos, Nigeria._

[Reuben Balik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/reuben-balik/) was the first engineer at Hologram. He led the integrations with some of the worst telco APIs from Verizon, Telus, Deutsche Telekom, and TIS into a unified SIM card platform.

[Q Carlson](https://www.linkedin.com/in/qcarlson/) was the 2nd designer at Flexport and has crafted beautiful experiences in messy, hard industries like supply chain. He uses design to differentiate — attracting a premium for the product and accelerating growth.

[Derrick Wolbert](https://www.linkedin.com/in/derrickwolbert/) ran the GTM team at Hologram from zero through Series B. Before Hologram, he navigated complex bureaucracy at Jeep/Chrysler, building the infotainment platform Waymo relies on in their vehicles.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79553&key=user_uploads/1452570/b005abd6-ee98-4c73-b11d-cb69a5067edb)

_Numo founders in Dogpatch 👆_

# 

# Ask

Are you using international contractors in your business? Ask them to invoice you using [Numo](https://numohq.com)!

We’re live in Nigeria. With Kenya, South Africa, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines coming very soon.\
\

launches.body:
# **The Problem**

Every day, crucial decisions are made based on outdated geospatial simulations. 

Insurance companies guess more than they would like about hurricane risks. Airports can't predict tomorrow's delays, let alone next week's. Meanwhile, utilities are crossing their fingers every heatwave that the grid won't collapse.

Earth’s simulation infrastructure needs an upgrade.

# **The Solution**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83141&key=user_uploads/1992622/3f194f0b-cfe1-4af7-a41a-e12d0d081aa7)

Today, [Silurian](https://silurian.ai/) is announcing the launch of GFT (Generative Forecasting Transformer), a 1.5B frontier model that simulates global weather up to 14 days ahead at approximately 11km resolution with unprecedented accuracy. Our model outperforms numerical weather prediction systems from the American (NOAA) and European (ECMWF) agencies by up to 30% across multiple variables. 

Remember Hurricane Beryl? In a simulation (shown above) run on the 1st of July, GFT correctly predicted that the hurricane would hit Texas. In contrast, the NOAA and ECMWF models wrongly predicted a landfall in Mexico, as [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/07/29/science/ai-weather-forecast-hurricane.html) recently reported. 

GFT is immediately available to our customers via our **Artificial Planetary Intelligence (API)**. The API allows users to easily query our models at any location on Earth, and it will become publicly available in the next few weeks. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83141&key=user_uploads/1992622/aadb6eff-4273-443f-abab-ff9244da3dcf)

GFT is only the beginning. We are working towards state-of-the-art simulation infrastructure for verticals such as energy, climate, and agriculture.

# **Team**

We are a team of scientists and engineers with years of experience in building large-scale AI simulations at Microsoft Research and Google Brain. Our work on weather and atmospheric chemistry simulations at Microsoft has been featured in [Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-01677-2), [Bloomberg,](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-25/from-trump-to-ai-bill-gates-sees-climate-impacts-for-the-world) and [The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-is-learning-to-predict-the-weather-8968fa7c?st=d0o2so2v9r14bf2&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink).

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd9eEb9mwTRMRPXQpJ6vkWtFRoUpGCc5sXpXIukdbAGyLsmWCAoqAKCOwXLbWfQZuFuGxg4Mu6qNyRHpIsoRKYlhDbnr8Qx0XCnUl26oa_T2ftzOsL4W3BijCebKj6OXA4oUoXWDnrqjJnqDIvGJz-SP5RL?key=P6HArdzTsIyNOARHbY8cEw)

# **Our Ask**

Do you want to talk about the weather? Reach out to us at [founders@silurian.ai](mailto:founders@silurian.ai)!

launches.title: Benchify: Instant self-healing codegen
launches.tagline: Fix & bundle your generated code at lightspeed
launches.body:
### **TL;DR**

Benchify handles the middle mile of codegen ensuring that generated code just works and is instantly executable. It’s a one-line SDK call between LLM clients and sandboxes to deliver instant code repair, accelerated bundling, and observability.

### **Who**

Anyone depending on non-human-in-the-loop codegen: – app builders, dynamic websites, agents, etc.

### **Problem**

Generated code breaks — constantly.

On top of normal bugs like duplicate function calls, parse errors, or missing or extra parens, AI systems introduce new ones, such as stray tool calls, /\* rest of code goes here \*/, and malformed diff applications. Running that code inside sandboxes only compounds the pain: every piece has to be perfect for execution to succeed, and the sandbox boot time delays the inevitable. Since all the sandboxes are just firecracker VMs designed to run anything, they’re not optimized for the common workflows builders actually care about. The result is slow setup, fragile execution, and painful feedback loops.

* **Missed errors**: Users hit error screens as soon as code loads in the browser. 
* **Delayed generations**: LLM-based auto-healing stretches generation times, slowing iteration.\
  **Token burn**: Edge-case failures trigger endless retries that chew through tokens without progress.  Often bugs are inherently out-of-distribution and thus hard to fix with AI.
* **Setup lag**: Sandboxes take 30-120s to boot before code even runs, adding cold-boot lag to the rep-cycle when there’s an error.
* **Lost data:** Sandboxes don’t easily track errors and the errors or only show the first (breaking) bug, making it hard to detect all the errors in code at once to push improvements 
* **Templates:** The use of templates speeds up sandboxes but leads to even more brittleness as the template has to be in perfect lockstep with the codegen.

 

### **Solution**

Benchify combines **non-AI techniques** (static analysis + program synthesis) with **highly optimized infrastructure** to deliver _turn-key code_ — fixed and bundled — in O(1 second).

It drops in as a **one-line SDK call** between your LLM client and the sandbox. If you’re only doing front-end work, you can skip the sandbox entirely and render directly from Benchify’s bundled output.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94193&key=user_uploads/1661832/dcd85900-d61c-47e4-b71e-0ef6244e5fd0)

**Code Repair**: Sub second fixes for parsing, dependency, CSS/Tailwind, type, and interaction errors (e.g. empty-Select) with more on the way. If there’s an issue you’re running into, let us know and we can add a fix!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94193&key=user_uploads/1661832/5d3a354c-69ee-4f5c-8437-0d0360f28874)

**Bundling**: Build and dependency resolution in 1-3s.

* _Front-end_: Returns code that instantly renders on client via our SDK.
* _Full-stack_: Bundles code that executes in any sandbox (skipping slow dependency & build steps) — the only delay left is sandbox cold boot.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94193&key=user_uploads/1661832/10606bbc-8df4-43f8-a574-aa9f0bd97d26)

**Observability**: Analytics on error patterns in generated code.

**Product Demo** 

https://youtu.be/my7yzpp8AqY

### **How it works**

Benchify’s analysis engine detects bugs and dispatches them to a growing library of static repair strategies in a fraction of a second. Strategies are optimized for different bug types, and layered using an incremental parsing approach, since sometimes fixing one bug unlocks others.  Each candidate fix is re-analyzed, with the best one selected automatically provided it yields a strict improvement in the code.  The architecture builds on prior research in _program synthesis_ and _program repair_, where the idea is to have a collection of strategies that may or may not work at fixing different bug types, combined with an analysis and execution engine that can efficiently determine whether or not a strategy succeeded.

### **Story**

We entered YC with a formal-methods-driven code review product. But unreliable LLM-generated test harnesses kept breaking it. Talking with builders made it clear: **the real bottleneck was brittle codegen itself.** We pivoted to focus entirely on making generated code self-healing.

### **Ask**

We’re focused on app builders today, but our core tech generalizes: agents, self-updating sites, programmatic ads, and more.

If generated code is slowing you down, let’s talk.

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83014&key=user_uploads/1661832/cb65a61c-fa84-4ccf-a1d5-2f6bf33b88fa)

# TL;DR

[Benchify](https://www.benchify.com/) is a code review tool that uncovers real bugs by actually running your code on strategically generated inputs, using methods typically restricted to rocket science and chip design.  When errors are found, Benchify provides verified bugs, unit tests, and a patch (coming soon).

# The problem

Engineers (like you) spend almost half their time testing and debugging, which, let’s be honest, they’d rather spend doing literally anything else.

* **Lower velocity:** Projects are delayed by testing & debugging
* **Site outages:** Despite all the effort, critical errors slip through, leading to site outages and other failures
* **Low test coverage:** Developing exhaustive tests is nearly impossible and generally put off for later…
* **Shallow test depth:** Testing is limited to a few hard-coded cases

# The solution

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83014&key=user_uploads/1661832/ed5d818b-cba4-41cf-9ca7-f9b9ca419737)

We test your code using _magic_ (ok, formal methods) and deliver the results in an actionable comment on your PR.

* **Automatic logical blueprint:** Benchify automatically writes a blueprint that says how your code is intended to function
* **Run thousands of tests:** Benchify tests your code against the blueprint using thousands of strategically generated inputs
* **Provide counterexamples:** Concrete, minimal counterexamples are provided when code fails so you can easily debug
* **Generate unit tests:** We automatically translate counterexamples into unit tests for easy reproducibility and test-driven development
* **Propose solutions:** When Benchify detects an error, it attempts to propose a solution, which it subjects to the same battery of tests as the original code

## Does it work?

The testing techniques Benchify uses are typically leveraged for mission critical use cases, such as silicon chip design, rocket engineering, and high-speed trading. Our secret sauce is in making these techniques usable and actionable. 

# The Team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83014&key=user_uploads/1661832/09a8c140-f845-4f96-9113-6daac4963be2)

Max and Juan first met as bright-eyed freshmen at Dartmouth College almost a decade ago and have been fast friends and on-and-off roommates since.  They’re deeply passionate about software assurance (who isn’t?) and excited to test your code.

* [**Max**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/max-von-hippel-3b90742a8/) holds a PhD in Computer Science from Northeastern University, focused on security and interactive theorem proving. He has worked at NASA, the DoD 😉, and Galois. Most importantly, he holds a Blue Belt from 10th Planet Jiu Jitsu. 
* [**Juan**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/juan-castano97/) built and sold a business, helped companies like Instawork and Klaviyo grow, and advised on deals at McKinsey. Juan double-majored in Economics and survival skills at Dartmouth (okay, the second one isn’t official), and later picked up an MBA from MIT, where he unfortunately missed out on a chance to test his skills with the [pirate certificate](https://physicaleducationandwellness.mit.edu/about/pirate-certificate/).

# Asks

* Hop on a [call](https://calendly.com/d/cpyy-ffc-ynf/juan-max-30-min) with us to try out Benchify or talk about your frustrations with software testing
* [Try out](http://www.benchify.com) our beta code reviewer and give us feedback
* Shoot us an email at [hello@benchify.com](mailto:hello@benchify.com) with your biggest backend software testing pain points, and we’ll see if we can help out!

Hello from Greg, Max and the Parsewise team! 👋

# **TL;DR**

[Parsewise](https://www.parsewise.ai/api?utm_source=launchyc&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=api_launch) turns multiple documents into a single structured response. Cross-document entity linking, contradiction detection, bounding boxes and UI toolkit to show it all included.

[See it live!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F1cSuZal03s)

**The Problem**

Today, you have to build and maintain complex document processing pipelines with changing business rules. You parse, classify, and rely on structured responses from LLMs or IDP tools (e.g., Reducto) to get individual extraction results that you piece together with other bits of information. There’s no reliable way to catch when information contradicts itself, which is risky. Finally, you build a custom verification UI for your operations team to deal with LLM mistakes.

**The Solution**

We provide an API to abstract all that away into a single call. You provide multiple documents and the desired output to get back a response with resolved values, flagged contradictions, and full traceability across documents / pages that you can display in your own app.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101959&key=user_uploads/1910315/a837442e-b7af-4113-acfd-699fc5074dff)

**Story Time**

Why are we working on this, how we got to where we are, who we are working with, and where we are headed.

Greg was at Palantir trying to make sense of various Japanese insurance documents and realizing that any processing pipeline built around it was highly custom, time-consuming, and brittle. Max was on the human operator side at Bain & Co, realizing that the technology was being held back due to a trust problem.

We realized that there is this powerful new capability for general reasoning (and thus processing). Models are getting extremely good at interpreting complex documents (shout-out to the Gemini model family) and perform better than most OCR-type solutions on the market.

So we set out to build the layer that comes on top:\
1\. Provide mapping from user intent to a dynamic ontology\
2\. Use the now-abundant intelligence to reason across documents to get to the right results\
3\. Provide the provenance trace and validation UX that is required in many use cases

We are working with leading customers, both small and large, like UBS, Compre Group, Thinksurance, and more. They rely on Parsewise to streamline submission intake, claim portfolio risk assessment, etc., for both API based integrations and operational workflows.

With this launch, we are inviting developers to build more reliable and delightful workflows around their unstructured data processing. As we scale, we are excited to be helping with the end-to-end integration and deterministically filling forms, mapping to 3rd party APIs and web portals.

\
See more at [https://www.parsewise.ai/api](https://www.parsewise.ai/api?utm_source=launchyc&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=api_launch)

_We hesitated between rap and insurance…_

Previously, we hit $1M in annual revenue building insurance workflows for brokers. Then we realized **the bigger opportunity was replacing them.**

In the US, there are 36 million SMBs, and 77% are underinsured because distribution is broken. Brokers can’t serve low-premium SMBs profitably: a $2K policy takes almost as much work as a $20K one.

Kinro changes that. Our AI agents handle the full broker workflow 24/7, from finding prospects to binding policies.

In 3 weeks, we got licensed in 30 states, appointed by 15 carriers, and **we bound the first-ever autonomously sold insurance policy.**

Before Kinro, [Pierre-Alexandre](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pakamienny/) was an AI researcher at DeepMind (post-training Gemini on financial services). [Parth Ainampudi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/partha42/) led ML infra at Zoox and I was Chief Insurance Officer at an MGA (insurtech).

**Asks**

If you ever need commercial insurance and want us to shop for you, hit us at [kinro.com](http://kinro.com) (yes we bought the domain for $25k, story [here](https://x.com/pierrealexai/status/2060382045571072043))! 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103281&key=user_uploads/2043734/bac0ad88-22f1-4376-accb-852778c22c1e)

_Post-pivot, Kinro goes to Atlanta to work for 48 straight hours with a retail broker specialized in selling to residential contractors._

**Q&A**

_“Why pivot?”_

We entered YC with a signed $1M enterprise sale to the 2nd largest auto-insurance comparator in the US a few days before (and a third of that money was wired). 

First OH, [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) asked us _“Why not become a broker directly?”_. 

We told him we thought we could reproduce that sale with other brokers and maybe carriers. A month in, we hadn’t yet reproduced the same feat (though we had secured a pilot with the 3rd insurance broker on Earth: WTW). It became more and more obvious that integrations were deep (and FDE intensive) and enterprise sales were endless.

What felt most off was the gap between what we were doing and our long-term vision: helping small business owners and individuals find the right insurance, wherever they are and whenever they need it.

_“So why not just build that?”_  \
\
We always knew we would eventually. Selling to brokers gave us a way to learn while getting paid. But we realized we weren’t learning as fast as we would by building directly for the people we ultimately wanted to serve.

1.5 months later, we came back to him _“Nicolas, we want to become brokers… and this $1M is bad for us”_, he simply answered _“Oh I told you guys, this was obvious”_ (LOL). Walking away from >1M+ from all our clients felt easier after talking about this to [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) and [@Mathilde Collin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/43195). Without YC, we would have waited much longer.

_“What types of insurance do you sell?”_

We sell small business insurance (General Liability, Business Owner’s policy, Worker’s compensation, Commercial Auto…). We focus on admitted markets where checking carriers' appetite and getting quotes can be fully automated with no communication with carriers.

**This new launch video as embarrassing as it is is worth watching! Send us a text if you want your angels to take care of your business.**

launches.tagline: We built a computation layer for health insurance that predicts the lowest true-cost coverage for anyone. We will be the national standard for how America chooses coverage, with the only engine that knows both what plans cost and what they actually do.
launches.body:
Hey everyone — we're **Chang and Bryan**, the founders of **Insurf**.

American health insurance is f\*\*\*ed: chosen by guesswork, enforced by denial. We built the engine that fixes both halves.

**TL;DR**

**Surely** computes the lowest-cost plan for anyone. **Inveto** fights denials for real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California, and each contract-authorized, de-identified outcome becomes coverage data nobody else has. Everything Inveto learns, Surely knows.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl/view?usp=sharing)

**The problem: America picks health plans from one number**

More than 20 million Marketplace enrollees choose coverage off the sticker premium. That guess is expensive.

• In our data, the lowest-premium plan was the lowest-cost option in **0 of 2,000 simulated years**.

• In one example, the cheaper sticker would have cost **$8,052 more** in a single bad year.

• That's one person. Multiply the risk across a family. Across a company.

• This year alone, **four million Americans** found out what their plans actually cost — and walked away from coverage.

We compute.

**Surely — the cost engine**

Surely ranks all plans by what they'll actually cost: premiums, deductibles, drug tiers, networks, out-of-pocket caps. Every number sourced from government filings.

**Inveto — the denial workbench**

Clinics upload a denial and the clinical record; Inveto produces source-cited, physician-signed appeals and supported prior authorizations. Live with real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California today.

**The moat is the join**

Every contract-authorized Inveto outcome becomes rights-cleared data about what plans actually do, including approvals, denials, appeals; Surely reads all of it. **What plans cost + what plans do. Nobody else has both.**

**Why now**

In 2028, health plans stop renewing automatically: 20 million+ people will re-choose coverage every single year — the largest forced re-shop in the history of American health insurance. $150 billion a year in premiums, re-decided annually.

And employers are next. The federal government projects **800,000 companies and 11 million+ people** will switch to ICHRA, where employees choose their own plans. That's a **trillion-dollar shift**. With Insurf, employers can expect to save **\~$5,000 per employee, per year**.

**Who we are**

Two friends who met during orientation at Brown. Chang got into medical school at 17, then worked a pharmacy counter watching thousands of people pay out of pocket for what they were promised. Bryan placed internationally in CS and physics competitions and has published IEEE research since high school.

**Our ask**

• Tired of overpaying for health insurance?

• Weighing ICHRA, or trying to cut your company's benefits spend?

• Running a specialty clinic buried in denials and prior auths?

See how much your company can save here: [insurf.io/audit](https://www.insurf.io/audit) or email [founders@insurf.io](mailto:founders@insurf.io) — we'll show you exactly what you'd save.

**Everyone sells plans. Nobody prices them. We compute.**

launches.tagline: Veltha reduces six hours of adjuster work to 10 minutes, with adjusters still making the final call
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Veltha reads an entire claim file, flags what's missing, and applies the exact federal regulation that governs it, producing a citation-backed determination a human adjuster just signs off on. Work that took an adjuster \~6 hours now takes \~10 minutes.** Starting with workers' comp and crop insurance.

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

1 in 4 claims adjusters expect to retire within five years. Experienced adjusters are retiring faster than carriers can replace them, and processing capacity is now the binding constraint on growth.

**What we built**

Veltha is an AI claims adjuster that runs the whole file end to end:

* **Triage** - reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection** - checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review** - applies the relevant federal rulebook, and produces a determination where **every output element is tied to a source span and a specific regulatory provision.**

The adjuster's job shifts from _doing_ the claim to _reviewing_ Veltha's output. Less chasing. Faster decisions. Output that survives an audit.

**What we understand that others don't: regulation is the moat, not the obstacle.** Horizontal platforms (Guidewire, Duck Creek) and generic AI-claims startups can summarize a claim file. They can't tell you _which_ provision triggered _which_ adjustment, with citations. We treat the federal rulebook as an anchor for the workflow we embed within the organisation. That's the difference between a summary a human re-does from scratch and an output an adjuster will actually sign.

**Our ask**

* **Anyone in claims at a carrier, MGA, or TPA** - especially **workers' comp**
* **People at large self-insured employers** with claims-heavy, high-risk workforces - Companies exactly like these are who we're built for: **Disney, Marriott, Ford, PG&E, Caterpillar**. If you know someone at that kind of company, an intro is gold.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Qlo uses AI agents to run commercial underwriting operations from submission to renewal. We rebuilt the underlying system so agents can operate across the entire workflow, not sit beside another legacy system. One enterprise client signed a two-year contract, went live in May, and has since tripled weekly primary quote throughput. The end state is autonomous underwriting that follows each company’s underwriting judgment and stays within the carrier’s appetite.

Today, we’re launching the **Qlo Inbox Agent**.

<https://youtu.be/aICb20uhqhU>

### The Problem

More than $110B in commercial insurance premium flows through U.S. MGAs every year. Much of the work still begins with an email from a broker.

Commercial underwriters can spend up to 80% of their day in the inbox, chasing missing applications, loss runs, and other submission documents. Even a submission with roughly $50K in annual premium can take 48 hours to turn into a quote.

Once the information arrives, teams still need to prepare the data, run the rater, and assemble the right endorsements and quote variants.

When volume grows, teams add headcount. But underwriting judgment is hard to train and keep consistent. Costs rise, good submissions remain untouched, and inconsistent decisions can hurt loss ratios.

More premium left on the table, now with more people on payroll.

### What We Built

Qlo runs the commercial underwriting workflow from submission to renewal. Specialized agents handle each operational step, while supervisor agents coordinate the work and communicate with the underwriter.

The Inbox Agent is one of those supervisors. An underwriter can message it from a phone like a teammate. It understands the instruction, calls the right subagents, and completes the work inside Qlo.

**The underwriter makes the call. The agents make it happen.**

One of those subagents is the Rater Converter we launched on Bookface. It turns an existing rating spreadsheet into a validated digital worksheet the rest of the workflow can use.

This is what agent-compatible means to us: agents understand the workflow, have the right context, and can act across the system. Today, they execute the underwriter’s decisions. The end state is autonomous underwriting within each company’s judgment, appetite, and controls.

**The party has begun. Let the agents dance on top of Qlo.**

Guidewire and Vertafore helped define the last era of commercial insurance software. We’re building Qlo to define the next one.

### Why Us

Before Qlo, Ryan spent 2.5 years building a commercial insurance marketplace and saw carrier-side systems up close. The company received acquisition terms from a public insurance company, and two founders who were customers there are now advisors to Qlo.

Liv previously led backend at a Taiwanese baby-monitor company generating roughly $15M in annual revenue. Ryan and Liv had already built together before starting Qlo.

We build alongside experienced underwriters who want to help define how commercial insurance will operate in the AI era.

### Our Ask

We’re looking for:

* **Introductions to commercial MGAs and program administrators**, especially submission-heavy programs with complex rating files or underwriting teams hitting the limits of their current systems.
* **Introductions to investors who understand commercial insurance** and see the same path toward autonomous underwriting.
* **Insurance operators with strong opinions about the future of underwriting**. Even if you’re not looking for a new system, we’d still like to learn how your business works.

If you run an MGA or program, want to build with us, or see the same future as an investor, email us at [founders@getqlo.com](mailto:founders@getqlo.com).

Commercial insurance moves slowly because **distribution beats architecture**.

But distribution eventually stops scaling when the architecture underneath it no longer works.

The system that solves the real problem will be adopted. Time will tell.

We’ll keep building.

launches.body:
**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. This year many insurance companies stopped covering risks that involve AI. We find the insurers that will still cover it, translate what you're building into terms they can price, and read every clause before anything is signed.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4>

**The problem**

Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.

For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.

The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.

**Why now**

Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own. 

**What we do**

We handle the whole coverage process end to end.

You send us an application. We take what you're building and put it in terms an insurance company can understand and price.

Then we go to market. We have access to hundreds of insurance companies, the ones that actually write this kind of risk, and we take your file to them. Most will pass. The few that want it compete on price and terms, and we keep shopping until every requirement you have is met, including the limits your customer contracts demand.

When offers come back we read the policies line by line. If an AI exclusion is attached, we push to get it removed, or we find a company that writes the AI coverage in on purpose. Then we tell you in plain terms what you've got.

We cover the lines your company actually needs: general liability, umbrella, property, equipment in transit and on customer sites, workers' comp, professional liability, management liability, and cyber.

You never pay us. The insurance company pays us a commission out of the premium when a policy is placed, so applying costs you nothing and there's no additional fee from us at any point.

**Where this goes**

Physical AI is expanding faster than any industry, and every company in it buys insurance every year for as long as it exists. The programs grow as the fleets grow.

We want to be the brokerage that grows with them: the people who know this risk best, hold the relationships with the markets that write it, and build the loss data of the future.

**Why us**

We're Sam and Alex, on leave from Harvard. We were already in insurance building models when we noticed that batch mates building some of the most innovative technology in the world couldn't get covered at all. Since then we’ve landed partnerships to offer these frontier companies easier access to better policies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110197&key=user_uploads/2666435/74c5c462-a2ff-44b8-ac6c-f8ebc7807dbd)


**The ask**

If you're building anything on the frontier, apply at[ risklytics.ai](http://risklytics.ai). It takes a few minutes, it costs nothing, and we'll come back with what the market says.

It doesn't matter what you have in place today. If you're building, we want to get you covered.

launches.tagline: Autonomously places hard-to-price risks in seconds
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Florin is a full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters. Software takes a submission from a raw intake form to a bindable quote in seconds. Instead of matching a business to a class code, it verifies what the business actually does using satellite imagery, permits, public records and social media, then prices it by simulating tens of thousands of ways its next few years could go.

<https://youtu.be/BaXtkdP6_nc>

**What we do and why**

Insurance prices risk with class codes. An underwriter receives an application PDF, matches the business to a row in a rate table, and quotes off that row. This breaks in two ways. Applications are incomplete or wrong, so the price is built on bad inputs. And when a business does not fit any row, either because it is genuinely new (robotics, AI, autonomy) or because the table says the whole class or state is unprofitable, the answer is a declination. That is why carriers are exiting entire states and why a three-year-old industry can barely buy coverage at any price.

Florin replaces the table with evidence. It ingests the submission directly, no intake team. It builds its own picture of the business from the outside: aerial imagery of the actual premises, permits and public records, even the insured's social media, where it has caught operations that were never disclosed on the application. From that verified picture it runs simulations of the business's possible futures and produces a quote you can bind in seconds. No human touches the file.

name: Ageospatial
long_description:
Ageospatial helps insurers value the risk on their properties remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.
one_liner: Helping insurance companies value risk on properties remotely.
